name: basic_subarray_containment
description: Session B [1,2,3] is a prefix of Session A [1,2,3,4,5], B should be removed

name: tail_subarray
description: Session B [3,4,5] is a tail (not prefix) subarray of Session A [1,2,3,4,5]. Under prefix semantics B is NOT redundant: a different first message means a different conversation root. Verified against full production data (2026-08-19): zero such pairs exist.

name: middle_subarray
description: Session B [2,3,4] is a middle (not prefix) subarray of Session A [1,2,3,4,5]. Under prefix semantics B is NOT redundant. Verified against full production data (2026-08-19): zero such pairs exist.

name: no_containment
description: No session is a prefix of another, nothing should be removed

name: identical_sessions_keep_earlier
description: Two sessions with identical MessageIDs, the one with larger ID should be removed

name: chain_containment
description: Session C is a prefix of B, B is a prefix of A; both B and C should be removed and merge into A

name: single_element_subarray
description: Single element session [3] is a mid subarray but NOT a prefix of [1,2,3,4,5], so it is kept. Verified against full production data (2026-08-19): zero such pairs exist.

name: non_contiguous_not_subarray
description: Session B [1,3,5] shares the first message with A [1,2,3,4,5] but is not a prefix of it

name: multiple_subarrays_of_same_parent
description: Only the prefix [10,20] is redundant. [30,40,50] (tail) and [20,30] (middle) start from a different message id, so they belong to other conversation roots and are kept.

name: empty_message_ids_ignored
description: Sessions with empty MessageIDs are ignored and not marked as redundant

name: single_session
description: Only one session, nothing to deduplicate

name: three_identical_sessions
description: Three sessions with identical MessageIDs, keep the one with smallest ID

name: cross_group_not_redundant
description: Sessions with different first message ids belong to different conversations and never dedup each other, even if one's ids are a contiguous subset of the other's.

name: forked_conversation
description: A conversation that forks: [1,2] is a prefix of both [1,2,3] and [1,2,4]. Only [1,2] is redundant; both branches are kept. Its ToolIDs merge into the first matching keeper (longest, then smallest id) = session 1.

name: merge_tool_ids
description: When session B is a prefix of A, B's tool_ids should be merged into A

name: merge_multiple_tool_ids
description: Only the prefix session [1,2,3] merges its tool_ids into the parent. [3,4,5] is a tail subarray with a different first message id, so it is kept and its tool_ids stay with it.

name: two_prefix_members_same_keeper
description: Two redundant members merging into the same keeper must accumulate, not overwrite, their ToolIDs.

name: group_keeper_protected_without_tools
description: The group keeper absorbed a redundant member, so it is a merge target and must be protected from the terminal rule even though every tool_ids is empty. Before this fix the keeper fell out of MergeMapping (both sides empty) and got deleted, wiping the whole conversation.

name: forked_keeper_not_protected
description: A fork branch that absorbed nothing is not a merge target, so the terminal rule still applies to it. Keeps parity with the pre-refactor behaviour.

name: singleton_terminal_tool_call
description: A lone snapshot whose last message is assistant+tool_calls is an interrupted branch and gets removed; its ToolIDs have nowhere to merge and are dropped.
